questionText: The major product formed when acetanilide undergoes bromination in presence of acetic acid is

options.explanation: Incorrect because tribromination occurs readily for free aniline in aqueous medium, not for acetanilide in acetic acid.

Correct because p-bromoacetanilide is the major product of this controlled bromination.

solution.quick: When acetanilide is treated with Br2 in acetic acid, the activating effect of the -NHCOCH3 group is controlled, yielding p-bromoacetanilide as the major product.
solution.concept: Acetanilide is less reactive than aniline because the lone pair on nitrogen is resonance-stabilized with the carbonyl group of the acetyl group. Bromination gives predominantly the para-isomer as the major product due to steric hindrance at the ortho position.

Step 2: Recognize that the lone pair on N is involved in resonance with the acetyl carbonyl group, reducing the activating power of the group compared to free aniline. Step 3: Carry out electrophilic substitution (bromination) using Br2 in CH3COOH. Step 4: The para-position is sterically more accessible and energetically favored over the ortho-position, forming p-bromoacetanilide as the major product.
